start.title: Ash That Should Be Cold
start.text: Grey ash streaks the snow beside the trail. When you touch it with the back of a finger, the powder is still faintly warm. A camp nearby was abandoned minutes ago.

buckets.flavourText: Three people left in a hurry, carrying weight. One circled behind before joining the others.
At least two people moved east. Their tracks are already softening.
The churned snow gives you more possibilities than answers.

watched.title: The Fourth Set of Prints
watched.text: The person who circled behind stood among the pines long enough to watch the road. Their prints face the exact place where you are kneeling.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice and spot the watcher

buckets.flavourText: A dark sleeve moves once between two trunks uphill.
You wait, but whatever watched the road has already withdrawn.

choices.text: Call out that you mean no trouble

watcher.title: Eyes Between the Trees
watcher.text: A thin man steps out with an unloaded crossbow held visibly low. He says the camp belongs to charcoal burners who do not appreciate patrols, thieves, or questions—in that order.

choices.text: Ask only whether the eastern path is safe

call.title: No Answer, Then One
call.text: For several heartbeats there is only wind. Then someone answers from uphill: "Depends what trouble means to you."

choices.text: Say you are only passing through

answer.title: Useful Hostility
answer.text: He tells you the eastern path is passable but warns of a washed-out footbridge. It is information given without friendliness, which may make it more reliable.

tracks.title: A Vanishing Camp
tracks.text: You follow the freshest prints for a short distance before they split deliberately over hard ground. Whoever left did not want the camp connected to their destination.

leave.title: Warm Ash, Cold Road
leave.text: You brush the ash from your glove and move on. By the time you look back, fresh snow is already covering it.
